newsitem.title: FRANCE: France hopes Italy, Spain able to join EMU in 1999.
newsitem.headline: France hopes Italy, Spain able to join EMU in 1999.

text.p: France hopes both Spain and Italy will be able to join European monetary union in 1999, a spokeswoman for President Jacques Chirac said on Monday.
Spokeswoman Catherine Colonna was speaking at a briefing ahead of a Franco-Spanish summit in Marseille which starts later on Monday.
"We hope that they will be there in 1999 while respecting the (Maastricht treaty) criteria," Colonna told a news conference.
She said France's attitude was the same for both Spain and Italy.

Chirac provoked a diplomatic row with Italy in early October by questioning whether Rome would be ready to join European economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1999. He later said he hoped Italy would indeed be ready in time.
Colonna said that Chirac, who was to hold talks later on Monday with Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar, would welcome Spain's efforts to cut its budget deficit.
"He would like Spain to be in a position to meet the convergence criteria (in 1999)," Colonna said.
She added the France hoped that the biggest number of EU countries possible would join EMU when the single currency is launched.
"The President will reaffirm France's determination to be there. It is in the interests of our country," she said.
The Franco-Spanish summit, which will also include finance, defence and foreign affairs ministers, was due to start in the southern French port of Marseille at 1625 GMT and runs into Tuesday morning.
